title: Name numeric state
prompt: Assign integer `elixir` equal to 10 and string `card` equal to X-Bow. Example: a numeric value uses no quotes.
starter:
# TODO: fix the types and values.
elixir = "10"
card = "Tesla"
tests:
assert type(elixir) is int and elixir == 10, "elixir must be the integer 10, not text"
assert card == "X-Bow", "card should name X-Bow"

title: Spend elixir
prompt: Given elixir 9 and cost 6, assign `remaining` by subtraction. Example: ten minus six would leave four.
starter:
# TODO: compute remaining from these inputs.
elixir = 9
cost = 6
remaining = 0
tests: assert remaining == 3, "9 elixir minus a 6-elixir X-Bow should leave 3"
hint: Use the variable names on the right side.

title: Regenerate and cap
prompt: Start at 9 elixir and wait 5.6 seconds at one elixir per 2.8 seconds. Assign `after` with a cap of 10. Example: starting at 3 would produce 5.0.
starter:
# TODO: include regeneration and the cap.
start = 9
seconds = 5.6
after = start
solution:
start = 9
seconds = 5.6
after = min(10, start + seconds / 2.8)
tests: assert after == 10, "9 plus 2 regenerated elixir must be capped at 10"
hint: Apply min to ten and the uncapped total.

title: Floor tower HP
prompt: A toy tower has 300 HP and takes 350 damage. Assign `remaining_hp` with a floor of zero. Example: 300 minus 100 would leave 200.
starter:
# TODO: prevent negative HP.
hp = 300
damage = 350
remaining_hp = hp - damage
solution:
hp = 300
damage = 350
remaining_hp = max(0, hp - damage)
tests: assert remaining_hp == 0, "Overkill should leave 0 HP, not a negative value"
hint: max chooses the larger of zero and the subtraction.

title: Format fractional elixir
prompt: Calculate `elixir = 3 + 1 / 2.8` and assign an f-string `report` displaying one decimal place as `Elixir: 3.4`. Example format specifier: `:.1f`. Keep elixir unrounded.
starter:
# TODO: keep numeric precision and format the report.
elixir = 3 + 1 / 2.8
report = "Elixir: unfinished"
tests:
assert abs(elixir - (3 + 1 / 2.8)) < 1e-12, "Keep the unrounded elixir value"
assert report == "Elixir: 3.4", "report should display one decimal: Elixir: 3.4"
hint: Format the display inside braces; do not round the stored state.
